After months of testing the Liquid Glass design, WhatsApp is expanding the rollout of its redesigned iPad app interface, including a brand-new Mac-style sidebar. Here's everything you need to know.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app interface

Although WhatsApp began adapting its iOS app for the major Liquid Glass visual overhaul back in October, the company spent several months before bringing this redesign to the iPad, kicking off limited beta testing in June.

As WABetaInfo reported at the time, the redesign brought Liquid Glass-styled tabs, buttons and context menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar familiar from the iPhone.

According to a new report from WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, switching the bottom tab bar by default to a brand-new Mac-style sidebar.

The sidebar mirrors the layout of the existing WhatsApp Mac version, offering quick access to chats, status updates, communities, calls, Meta AI and other parts of the app. Users can also hide the sidebar to give the chat list and conversation window more room.

Here's what the report says:

According to WABetaInfo, the new sidebar is now available to some beta testers running the latest TestFlight build, although some users on the standard App Store version have also started seeing the new interface.

As is customary with WhatsApp, it will take some time before the new interface reaches all users, whether they're on the beta or the stable release. Once it rolls out, however, iPad users will benefit from a layout that better suits how the tablet is used.
